svg.aria-label: Why the breakthrough curve narrows. (a) In an open-fracture network a tracer pulse races through a fast channel that holds little volume while much of it lingers in slow side fractures: early peak, long tail. (b) After channelization in a vein network the dissolved channel holds most of the pore space and most of the flow, so the pulse moves as a near-plug and arrives close to the mean residence time.
svg.text: (a) open-fracture network: the fast channel holds little volume
most volume in slow side fractures
(b) vein network after channelization: the channel holds most of the pore space
side fractures still filled: little volume, little flow
as the channel forms: median arrival rises towards τres (≈0.79 → 0.90), the tail steepens (γ ≈ 3.3 → 4.1), dispersivity falls
